newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Brazil to draw on coffee stocks to meet demand.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to draw on coffee stocks to meet demand.

text.p: Brazil will have to draw on its official coffee stocks, currently totaling 13.2 million 60-kg bags, to meet demand at home and overseas, said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (FEBEC).

Aranha, in Colombia for a regional coffee meeting, did not specify when the government-controlled stocks would be drawn on. But he said inventories in the hands of private exporters were "insufficient for the needs of the market."

"There will be a need to use part of the official stocks," he said. Aranha, who spoke in a brief Reuter interview on the sidelines of the meeting here, said FEBEC does not make forecasts about Brazil's coffee production.
But he stressed that official estimates for the 1997/98 coffee year were still set at 22 million 60-kg bags, down from 27 million in the 1996/97 coffee year.

Because of tight supply on world markets he predicted that current prices would hold "for a good while yet." He added that it was "important to know how to coordinate the situation" among world producers to avoid any sudden slip in prices, however.
